evidence: Interfaces CreateProductInput and PlaceOrderInput define use-case input contracts, which belong to the application layer.
Interfaces OrderDto and ProductDto define use-case output contracts, which belong to the application layer.
toOrderDto and toProductDto only copy fields from domain objects into DTOs and contain no business rules or I/O.
toProductDto maps product.availableStock straight to stock, so the stock calculation stays in the domain.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/application/dtos.ts holds only application-layer input/output data contracts (CreateProductInput, PlaceOrderInput, OrderDto, ProductDto) and simple mapping functions that turn domain entities into DTOs. It also has no business rules: the mappers only copy fields, and toProductDto reads the domain's own availableStock getter rather than computing stock itself.
